name: Insecure direct object reference
description:
The application uses an identifier supplied by the client (a numeric or UUID object id in the query string, the path, a cookie or a JSON body) to look up an object, and returns the object without checking that the authenticated user is allowed to see it. Changing the identifier to another valid value returns a different user's object.

This is broken object-level authorization (OWASP API Security Top 10 2023, API1). Its impact depends on what the objects hold: profiles, orders, invoices and documents commonly carry personal or financial data.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no insecure direct object reference entry. It is classified under CWE-639, a child of the CWE-284 class that Burp's 'Broken access control' row uses.
remediation:
Authorize every object access on the server against the authenticated identity, not against anything the client sends: look the object up through the current user's own scope (for example WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?), or check ownership or an explicit grant before returning it. Never decide authorization from a client-held user id, role or account cookie.

Unpredictable identifiers (random UUIDs) make enumeration harder but are not an access control; the ownership check is still required.
